title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In this third draft of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986), Grothendieck axiomatizes a tame-topological 'atelier' as an order-theoretic structure, without points. The data are as follows.
- M is a poset of 'lieux' (regions/loci) under inclusion ≤.
- ≪ is a 'well-inside' relation (X' ≪ X roughly means X' is relatively compact in, or contained in the interior of, X).
- Λ ⊂ M is a dense sub-collection, closed under ≤ by the next page.
- || is a separation/disjointness relation.

The page uses several 'shadow' sets attached to a lieu X:
- omb_Λ(X) is the shadow of X in Λ, presumably the elements Z ∈ Λ with Z ≪ X.
- Omb(X) is a larger version, presumably the elements of M below X.
- X̃ is the down-set of X.
- X'_Y := X̃' ∩ Omb(Y) is the 'trace' of X' on Y (margin NB).

Problem of the page. When does a system (M, ≤, ≪, Λ dense, ||), with || given only on Λ, come from an atelier satisfying At C_Λ? Here At C_Λ is the axiom, stated on p.43 and formalised on p.45, that compatibility (≯) / separation of two lieux X, Y is detected on all pairs of Λ-approximants X' ∈ comb_Λ(X), Y' ∈ comb_Λ(Y). Equivalently: can the relation || on M be reconstructed from its restriction to a dense base?

Axioms. The axioms MΛ0–MΛ3 (for ≤, ≪, Λ) are kept unchanged. Two axioms are added for || on Λ:
- MΛ'4: || on Λ is symmetric and antireflexive (X || X' implies X ≠ X'). It is also hereditary for ≪: if X || Y, X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y, then X' || Y'.
- MΛ'5 (a separation axiom): let Y ≤ X, Y' ∈ omb_Λ(Y) and X' ∈ omb_Λ(X). If X' does not meet Y, i.e. X'_Y = ∅, then X' || Y'.

The emptiness condition in MΛ'5 has several variants. He states a lemma, depending only on ≤, ≪, Λ and MΛ0–MΛ3, for Y ≤ X and X' ≪ X. Its four conditions are:
- (i) omb_Λ(Y) ∩ omb_Λ(X') = ∅;
- (i') Omb_Λ(Y) ∩ Omb(X') = ∅;
- (ii') Omb(Y) ∩ X̃' = ∅ (= X'_Y);
- (ii) omb_Λ(Y) ∩ X̃' = ∅.

The lemma says (i), (i') and (ii') are equivalent and imply (ii). The margin adds that (ii) is equivalent to the others only if Λ is 'very dense' (every X ∈ M contains some Z ∈ Λ, Z ≤ X).

The proof begins: '(i') ⇒ (i): suppose not (i); by MΛ1 one gets Y' in omb_Λ(Y) ∩ omb_Λ(X'), hence Y' ∈ X̃' ∩ …'. It breaks off at the bottom of the page.

The next page (24 June) repackages these conditions as AtΛ1–AtΛ3 / AtDΛ / AtCΛ(spec/pol). It then gives an implication diagram between them.
errors: The lemma's header claims (i),(i'),(ii') equivalent and imply (ii). This is consistent with the margin, which says (ii) is equivalent to them only under 'very density'. However, the boxed statement of MΛ'5 had earlier asserted 'tous se valent' (all variants equivalent) without that hypothesis. Grothendieck himself corrects this in the lemma.
The proof of (i')⇒(i) is only begun on this page; the remaining implications are not proved here.
The hypothesis Y ≤ X in MΛ'5 seems unnecessary for the conclusion as formulated, since only X'_Y is used. It may be a vestige of the crossed-out version involving a common upper bound Z.

ideas.what: Point-free axiomatization of tame topology via a poset of 'lieux' with a well-inside relation ≪ and a separation relation ||
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / contact algebras / proximity (de Vries) algebras; region-based theory of space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Vries (1962), Clarke (1981), Düntsch–Vakarelov, Dimov–Vakarelov (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for 'tame topology' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the atelier axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Reconstructing the separation relation on all lieux from its restriction to a dense sub-collection Λ (a base), with hereditary and separation axioms MΛ'4, MΛ'5
ideas.modern_name: Extension of a proximity/contact relation from a dense subalgebra (base) of a contact algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in contact-algebra literature (e.g. Dimov–Vakarelov on dense subalgebras)

ideas.what: Lemma on equivalent 'non-meeting' conditions defined via shadows (omb, Omb, down-sets), with a 'very dense' hypothesis needed for full equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic lemma on disjointness of down-sets / regular-open approximations

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'atelier' axiomatics is in substance a mereotopology or contact algebra. It has a well-inside relation ≪, a disjointness relation ||, and a dense base Λ from which || is reconstructed. This was developed independently of, and roughly in parallel with, the region-based-space / contact-algebra literature, and the link between that literature and his tame-topology programme seems not to be made.
missed.quote: La question, c'est quand un système (M, ≤, <<, Λ⊂M, ||) avec Λ⊂M dense provient d'une structure d'AtD
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Contact-algebra duality theorems (de Vries, Dimov–Vakarelov) could supply representation theorems for Grothendieck's ateliers. Conversely, his tame-topology motivation (o-minimal-like 'lieux') could suggest new classes of contact algebras.

missed.claim: The characterization of when a (M, ≤, ≪, Λ, ||) system arises from an atelier satisfying AtC_Λ is posed but only partially worked out. The lemma's proof breaks off.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable order-theoretic problem within an unexplored point-free foundation for tame topology. Its interest is modest unless the whole atelier programme is revived.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in an unpublished point-free axiomatics of tame topology. The material is intrinsically little-known, but it is routine order-theoretic bookkeeping. The only notable aspect is the implicit parallel with contact algebras and mereotopology.
transcription_corrections: 'At C_∧ (type c)' should read 'At C_Λ (spec)', matching AtCΛ(spec) on p.45.
'Soient Y≤X {+∨∨ X'+}' should read 'Soient Y ≤ X ≫ X'' (i.e. X' ≪ X, written vertically under X).
'X'∈omb_Λ^{X'}(X)' should read 'X' ∈ omb_Λ(X)'; the superscript is a stray correction.
In MΛ'4 the parenthesis reads 'X || X' implique X ≠ X''.
Margin should read approximately 'Ou aussi AtD' (rather than 'AtD Ou ainsi?').
The final proof line begins '(i') ⇒ (i): Supposons non (i), prenons … par MΛ1 … omb_Λ(Y) ∩ omb_Λ(X') ∋ Y' …', followed by '= Y' ∈ X̃' ∩'.
